commit fcbb63c654404742b77d0a8d652ead04b1ad4190
feat: migrate wasm plugin runtime from wasmer to wasmtime

Replaces the wasmer crate with wasmtime (43.0.2) for compiling and running
Wasm format plugins.

- Host state now lives in the wasmtime Store (a WasmHostState enum reached via
  Caller) instead of wasmer's FunctionEnv; imports are registered on a Linker
  and memory is accessed via wasmtime::Memory.
- Native Cranelift codegen on x86_64/aarch64/riscv64/s390x. powerpc64,
  loongarch64 and android instead compile to wasmtime's portable Pulley
  bytecode (no native backend, and no signal-based traps in the Android
  sandbox), replacing the wasmi interpreter.
- Drops the corosensei dependency and the loongarch64 LLVM cross-image
  (Pulley is pure Rust via Cranelift), so loongarch64 now builds with plain
  cross. Removes the obsolete cross-image workflow and Dockerfile.
- Builds wasmtime with a minimal feature set to keep the binary size down.
- Sets max_wasm_stack to 1 MiB and runs each instance on a dedicated
  larger-stack thread (wasmtime's default overflows on deeply nested files).
- Renames the WASMER_COMPILER_VERSION cache key constant to WASM_CACHE_VERSION.

-/**
- * Image tag derived from the Dockerfile contents. Editing the Dockerfile
- * produces a new tag, so the image-build workflow republishes and ci.ts pulls
- * the matching image in lockstep (with a local build fallback for the PR that
- * introduces the change, before the new tag exists).
- */
-export const crossImageTag = await computeTag();

-async function computeTag() {

This will allow us to support many more architectures (ex. windows arm) and drop a lot of code. I checked the performance and it's equivalent.

--

Replaces the wasmer crate with wasmtime (43.0.2) for compiling and running Wasm format plugins.

- Host state now lives in the wasmtime Store (a WasmHostState enum reached via Caller) instead of wasmer's FunctionEnv; imports are registered on a Linker and memory is accessed via wasmtime::Memory.
- Native Cranelift codegen on x86_64/aarch64/riscv64/s390x. powerpc64, loongarch64 and android instead compile to wasmtime's portable Pulley bytecode (no native backend, and no signal-based traps in the Android sandbox), replacing the wasmi interpreter (which according to Wasmer, was not good and buggy. They've removed it).
- Drops the corosensei dependency and the loongarch64 LLVM cross-image (Pulley is pure Rust via Cranelift), so loongarch64 now builds with plain cross. Removes the obsolete cross-image workflow and Dockerfile.
- Builds wasmtime with a minimal feature set to keep the binary size down.
- Sets max_wasm_stack to 1 MiB and runs each instance on a dedicated larger-stack thread (wasmtime's default overflows on deeply nested files).
